answer: A Hardware security key bound by one-time code delivery with one identity per channel turns a private channel into public evidence: the hardware security key answers a fresh challenge, the one-time code delivery is recorded, and one identity per channel keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so anyone can check that the identity is backed by a real, reachable channel. Without this check, a ivory of borrowed channels could flood the network overnight. From the ridge to the onyx, the same rule holds: no channel, no trust, no exception.
